item.title: Yasaka Shrine: Gion's Lantern-Lit Guardian Shrine — Guide
item.description: Yasaka Shrine, sometimes called Gion-san, sits at the eastern end of Shijo street where it meets the Gion district and the slopes of Higashiyama. Founded over 1,300 years ago, it is one of Kyoto’s most popular shrines, its bright vermilion gate and main hall always open and free to enter, day or night. After dark its central dance stage glows with hundreds of paper lanterns donated by local businesses, and its grounds flow directly into Maruyama Park behind.

item.title: Gion Matsuri Guide: Kyoto's Greatest Festival
item.description: Gion Matsuri is the most famous festival in Japan — a spectacular, month-long celebration that takes over Kyoto every July. Centred on Yasaka Shrine and over 1,150 years old, it culminates in the magnificent Yamaboko Junko, grand processions of towering wooden floats — some over 25 metres tall and weighing several tonnes — hauled through the city by teams of men to the music of flutes, drums, and bells. In the evenings before the processions, the Yoiyama street parties fill the downtown with lantern-lit floats, food stalls, and crowds in yukata.
